exposure: socioeconomic factors (Child Opportunity Index, employment, private insurance)
cohort: The study analyzed 294 pregnancies resulting in live births from Black, Hispanic, and White women with multiple sclerosis or clinically isolated syndrome across 9 US MS centers between 2010 and 2021.
finding: Underrepresented women with MS entered pregnancy with higher disability and fewer healthcare resources, leading to babies with lower birthweights and shorter breastfeeding durations compared to White women.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery differed significantly by race, with Black women having the highest rates of emergency cesarean deliveries and Hispanic women the highest rates of uncomplicated vaginal deliveries.
followup_time: up to 6 months after birth (for breastfeeding duration)
birth_weight: Median birthweights were 3,198 g (for babies born to underrepresented women) vs 3,275 g (for babies born to White women).
